messages:
marta: Idea: let's add a tiny "cost lighthouse" panel in Console that highlights per-route per-model unit economics (avg cost/token), a small cache-scrub summary (tokens avoided by cache), and a single-line routing impact (delta when falling back). goal: quick signal for PMs and oncall without full billing joins.
li: Nice metaphor. We should be explicit about what "unit economics" means in the panel (e.g., median cost/token over last 1h vs invoice avg).
marta: yeah — show two numbers: short-window median (1h) and a 24h rolling avg. also show variance and a tiny confidence dot if we sampled.
samir: Implementation constraints: token_events is huge. Proposal: minute-level pre-agg MV that writes (route, model, minute, tokens_total, tokens_cached_winner, invocations, fallback_count, sample_factor). We can then compute efficient projections.
ben: Important: we must add cache "winner" semantics to the ingestion so we never double-count prefix + KV hits. That migration needs a plan for backfilling historical MVs.
li: How will sampling work? For many tenants we can't afford full resolution.
samir: Plan: deterministic top-k full-res (by 7-day spend), reservoir sampling per-tenant for medium spend, 0.5% for long-tail. Store sample_factor so UI can extrapolate and show confidence.
emma: UX: show a subtle confidence ribbon on the tile (green/orange/red) and a tooltip that explains sample factor + top-k vs extrapolated. Keep tile width ~280px.
ben: Queries: MV should include pre-computed effective_cost_per_token = cost_model(model_sku) * (1 - quant_adjust) / effective_batch_factor. Or we can compute cost client-side if cost_model changes. Thoughts?
li: Cost_model is versioned; better to store raw tokens and invocations in MV and let backend apply the latest cost model at read-time to avoid costly MV churn.
samir: Agreed. Store counts only. Backend: econ-service will join MV with a small cost-model table (tiny), compute effective cost and projection on the fly.
marta: Rollout UX: during canary we should render canary vs baseline columns with delta and a callout if projected 24h burn increases > 20%. Also a tiny "open cost inspector" link that drills into trace samples.
emma: And a "hide sampling" toggle for tenants that prefer sampled inference to be hidden. But default show confidence.
ben: Performance ops: infra should expose an endpoint /internal/econ/lighthouse?route=&since= that returns top-N models with pre-agg rows compressed. We need <=2m freshness SLA. Also pagination + allow tenant filter.
samir: I'll prototype the MV SQL: ```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW econ_minute_preagg AS
SELECT
  route_id
 ,model_sku
 ,date_trunc('minute', ts) AS minute
 ,SUM(tokens) AS tokens_total
 ,SUM(CASE WHEN cache_winner THEN tokens ELSE 0 END) AS tokens_cached_winner
 ,COUNT(1) AS invocations
 ,SUM((is_fallback)::int) AS fallback_count
 ,avg(sample_factor) AS sample_factor
FROM token_events
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY 1,2,3;
```
li: Good start. Need to ensure ingestion sets cache_winner deterministically (prefix wins over kv if both report? or vice versa per product decision). Document it.
ben: Backfill: run a best-effort job to compute tokens_cached_winner historically using logs, but mark backfill rows with a backfill flag so confidence is lower.
emma: For the tile copy: short title "Cost Lighthouse" subtitle "per-route unit economics" and microcopy on hover: "Median cost/token (1h) · 24h avg · cache saved tokens · fallback rate · sample confidence". Keep language non-accounting; call it "engineering signal".
devex-bot: NOTE: Automated rollback suggestion available if canary delta > 2x and fallback rate > 5%. Requires feature-flag 'econ-ops-suggestions' and IAM scope econ.rollback.
marta: Action items: samir add cache_winner + sampling metadata to ingestion (PR + migration plan), ben to prototype MV and pagination API stub, li to write a short doc on cache winner semantics, emma to mock tile and confidence ribbon, I'll draft a 1-pager and link to prototype.
li: I'll also add a small section on how to interpret extrapolated numbers vs invoice numbers.
samir: I'll start on MV and a small simulated dataset so UI can iterate without prod impact.
ben: I'll stub /internal/econ/lighthouse and return a canned payload for dev yesterday.
emma: I'll post mocks in #design later today.
marta: Thanks all. If anyone wants ownership of the rollback UX we should assign it now. Otherwise I'll shepherd the spec.
li: I'll take the rollback UX doc.
marta: perfect. I'll post the 1-pager in this thread tomorrow. :shipit:
